name: Vauxhall / Opel
description: Vauxhall / Opel over a generic OBD-II dongle, on 11-bit/500k High Speed GMLAN. Built for the GM Global A era (Astra K, Insignia B, Mokka X, Zafira C -- roughly 2010-2019). Global A does NOT speak plain UDS: fault codes are GMW3110 ReadDiagnosticInformation (0xA9), clear is 0x04 and identification is 0x1A, so the scan ladders both dialects and reports which one answered. Powertrain sits at 0x7E0/0x7E1 (response +8); body/chassis modules use GM's own 0x24x block (response +0x400). Low-Speed GMLAN (single-wire, pin 1) carries most comfort modules and is NOT reachable through any standard dongle. 2019+ Vauxhalls are PSA/Stellantis platforms, not GM -- use the Peugeot profile for those. Read-only apart from a confirm-gated fault clear.

panel.title: GMLAN module scan (OBD dongle)
panel.hint: Reads the engine and gearbox fault memory + identification deeper than generic OBD-II, plus the body/chassis modules that answer on GM's 0x24x block. Faults are shown GM-style as code + failure type (P0716-71). The module address list published for Global A is generic to GM, not confirmed per model, so use 'Find modules' first on a car you don't know -- it sweeps both address blocks and reports what actually answers. Pick the adapter top-right, ignition ON, then scan.

actions.label: Find modules
actions.busy: Sweeping the GMLAN diagnostic address blocks...
actions.title: Find this car's modules
actions.hint: Probes every address in the powertrain block (0x7E0-0x7E7, reply +8) and GM's body/chassis block (0x240-0x25F, reply +0x400) and reports which ones answer, which dialect they answered in, and what they call themselves. This is how you build a verified module map for a model nobody has published one for. Read-only.

actions.label: Software versions
actions.busy: Reading each module's flashed software identification...
actions.title: What software is in this car
actions.hint: Asks every module that answers for the calibration it is actually running: End Model Part Number, Base Model Part Number, Boot Software Part Number and Software Module Identifiers 01-10, each with its two-character alpha code, plus the date it was last programmed and the tester code that programmed it. Part numbers come out of GMW3110 as 4-byte binary and are shown as the decimal a parts catalogue quotes. This is the step before asking whether an update exists -- including a gearbox recalibration: take these numbers to the manufacturer's programming system and compare against what it offers for the VIN. Read-only. The harness reads calibrations, it does not write them.

actions.label: Gearbox live
actions.busy: Reading the gearbox and engine live values...
actions.title: Vauxhall gearbox + engine live
actions.hint: Reads the GM-native transmission DIDs on the TCM (0x7E1): fluid temperature, current gear and target/commanded gear -- decodes from the OBDb VauxhallOpel signalset (CC-BY-SA-4.0). Current vs target gear read together is the pair that shows a shift flare: the TCM commands 4th while the box is still in 3rd. Also flags whether transmission fluid temperature is inside the Fast Learn window, and adds a curated generic Mode-01 set (rpm, speed, coolant, oil temp, module voltage, ambient). No public DID exposes the TCM's clutch adaptive cells, line pressure or clutch slip -- those are GDS2-only and nothing is invented for them.
